state: OPEN — BLOCKS GRADUATION, does not block the B52 site-scoped discharge
finding: The reachable-obligation queue does not enumerate every extension-slot callback in the reachable source. Measured at candidate a8716b4f2: 114 `unsafe extern "C" fn` slot callbacks (i2s/i2r/i2v/r2i/s2i/v2i) exist in `src/`, but only 51 appear in the 312-obligation set; 63 are absent entirely. An absent site is not DISCHARGED and not BLOCKED: it is invisible, so it can neither be discharged nor refused. That is incompatible with the graduation condition that no safety-relevant unknown remains.

strongest_case.why_this_is_not_merely_unreachable: v3_skid.rs is unambiguously reachable: B50 discharged `skid_i2s` in the same file (B50-I2S-009), and that site appears in the closure. The same extension row also installs `s2i_skey_id` as its s2i callback, yet that callback is absent from the queue. A file being reachable is not the same as every slot in it being enumerated, and here the difference is a specific reachable production callback.

measured_evidence.closure: evidence/closure-ssh-b52-baseline.json (312 obligations, 177 DISCHARGED / 135 BLOCKED / 0 UNKNOWN, both families)
measured_evidence.scan: grep -rnE 'unsafe extern "C" fn (s2i|i2s|i2r|i2v|r2i|v2i)_' src/ -> 114 definitions; 51 present in .obligations, 63 absent
measured_evidence.not_claimed: The 63 are NOT all claimed to be reachable. The claim is narrower and sufficient to block graduation: the queue does not enumerate them, and reachability has not been established per site. Some are plausibly unreachable from ssh/sshd; that must be shown, not assumed.

why_it_matters_for_graduation: `SAFE_COMPATIBLE` requires every applicable mechanism to be SAFETY_DISCHARGED and no safety-relevant unknown or blocked obligation to remain. A site absent from the queue is an unknown that the ledger cannot represent.
A discharge receipt for a family ('the s2i family', 'the i2r printers') cannot be complete if the family is defined by the queue rather than by the source.
The B52 review found this by comparing source registrations to the queue; that comparison is reproducible and must become a gate, not a one-off observation.
required_resolution: Add an enumeration-completeness gate: for every reachable file, every extension-slot callback and every `#[no_mangle] extern "C"` definition must appear in the obligation set, or carry a recorded reachability exclusion with evidence (a caller-path argument, not an assertion).

Classify each of the 63 absent sites as REACHABLE (enrol it in the queue with a stable identity and BLOCKED status) or UNREACHABLE-FROM-THESE-CONSUMERS (record the caller-path evidence and the consumer identity it was established against).
Re-run both closures after the enrolment; counts will move, and that movement must be reported, not suppressed.
Independent adversarial review of the gate, including a negative control: remove one callback from the enumeration and confirm the gate fails.
Do not treat this finding as discharged by B52's approval: B52's nine sites are individually sound, but the family name must not be read as exhaustive.
non_claims: This is not a defect in the nine B52 sites, all of which were verified at their coordinates with enforced liveness and a reproduced canary.
It is not a claim that all 63 absent sites are reachable, and it is not a claim that any specific absent site is unsafe.
It does not by itself change the applied ledger; the B52 row is site-scoped and names only its nine boundaries.
